title: Providence phrases that offended: efficacious providence, physical impulse, judicial acts
pass_a_gloss: Men took offense at some phrases excerpted from the writings of Zwingli, Martyr, Calvin, Beza, Zanchi, Rennecher, Piscator, &c., by which those Theologians meant, with Holy Scripture, (1) God's efficacious Providence around evils & the evil, from the phrases of hardening, blinding, sending a spirit of lying, handing over into a reprobate mind, drawing a callus over, sending the ἐνέργεια / efficacy of error, &c.; (2) a motion of sinning causes or an impulse — not indeed moral, but physical — as we all are moved in God, just as He sent Joseph (Gen. 45:7; 50:20), impelled Shimei to curse (2 Sam. 16:10), the prophets of Ahab to deceive and lie (1 Kings 22:22–23), &c.; (3) finally God's acts, in this whole Providence around the wicked, as judicial & penal — either for penalty of one's own crime in Pharaoh, unbelieving Jews, Judas the traitor, &c., or for penalty of another's crime, such as Absalom incest, Jeroboam schism, the lying spirit about to lead Ahab on, &c.
pass_b_english: Men took offense at certain phrases drawn from the writings of Zwingli, Martyr, Calvin, Beza, Zanchi, Rennecher, Piscator, and others. By those phrases the Theologians meant, with Holy Scripture, three things.

First: God's efficacious Providence around evils and around the wicked — spoken of in the biblical phrases of hardening, of blinding, of sending a lying spirit, of handing over into a reprobate mind (Romans 1:28), of drawing a callus over, of sending the ἐνέργεια — the working — of error (2 Thessalonians 2:11), and the like.

Second: a motion, or impulse, of sinning causes — not a merely moral one, but a physical one — seeing that in God we all are moved: as when He sent Joseph (Genesis 45:7; 50:20), drove Shimei to curse (2 Samuel 16:10), and drove Ahab's prophets to deceive and to lie (1 Kings 22:22–23), and so on.

Third: God's acts in this whole Providence around the wicked are judicial and penal — either as penalty for one's own crime, as in Pharaoh, in the unbelieving Jews, in Judas the traitor, and the like; or as penalty for another's crime, such as Absalom's incest, Jeroboam's schism, and the lying spirit that was to lead Ahab on, and so on.
source_text: Offenderunt Viri ad phrases nonnullas, excerptas ex scriptis Zwinglii, Martyris, Calvini, Bezae, Zanchii, Rennecheri, Piscatoris, &c. quibus illi Theologi cum Scripturâ S. voluerunt 1. Providentiam Dei efficacem circa mala, & malos, ex phrasibus, indurandi, excæcandi, indendi Spiritum mendacii, tradendi in reprobum sensum, callum obducendi, mittendi ἐνέργειαν efficaciam erroris, &c. 2. Motionem causarum peccantium vel impulsionem, non certè moralem, sed physicam, ut qui omnes in Deo movemur, prout misit Josephum, Gen. XLV. 7. L. 20, impulit Simehum ad maledicendum 2. Sam. XVI. 10. Prophetas Achabi ad decipiendum, mentiendum, Reg. XXII. 22. 23. &c. 3. Tandem actus Dei, in hac omni Providentia circa malos, judiciales & penales, seu in poenam delicti proprii in Pharaone, Judaeis incredulis, Juda proditore, &c. seu in poenam delicti alieni, qualis fuit incestus Absalomi, Schisma Jeroboami, spiritus mendax inducturus Achabum, &c.
